Namaste! Early blight causes dark, target-like spots on lower leaves, which spreads fast in Kochi's humid weather. 

To control it effectively:
1. **Sanitation:** Immediately prune and destroy infected lower leaves, and avoid splashing water on foliage by using drip irrigation.
2. **Chemical Spray:** Spray Mancozeb (2g per liter of water) or Copper Oxychloride (3g per liter) thoroughly on the crop. Repeat after 10-12 days if needed.
3. **Organic Option:** You can spray Neem oil (5ml per liter of water with a bit of soap) as a preventive measure. 

Ensure good plant spacing across your 2.5 acres to allow air circulation and reduce moisture build-up!

Namaste! In Kochi's humid climate, black spots on tomatoes are usually caused by fungal Early Blight (on leaves and stems) or Calcium deficiency (if the spots are dark and sunken at the bottom of the fruit). 

If the spots are on the leaves, prune the infected lower leaves immediately and spray **Mancozeb** (2 grams per liter of water) or **Copper Oxychloride** (3 grams per liter). If the spots are only at the bottom of the fruit, spray **Calcium Nitrate** (5 grams per liter) on the plants. Always water at the base of the plant rather than spraying overhead to keep the leaves dry. 

Would you like to send a description of where the spots are located so I can help you identify the exact cause?
Why are my tomato leaves turning yellow?

Namaste! Leaf yellowing in tomatoes is usually caused by overwatering, nitrogen deficiency, or fungal infections like Early Blight, which are common in Ernakulam's humid climate. 

If the older bottom leaves turn pale yellow first, your plants likely need nitrogen—apply well-rotted cow manure or a balanced NPK (19:19:19) fertilizer. If you see yellowing with dark brown spots, it is likely a fungal attack, so ensure good field drainage and spray Neem oil (5 ml per liter of water) or Copper Oxychloride (2 grams per liter). 

Are the leaves curling, or is the yellowing only at the bottom or top of the plant? Let me know so I can help you fix it quickly!

Namaste! Black spots on tomatoes are commonly caused by **Early Blight** (a fungal disease) or **Blossom End Rot** (calcium deficiency). 

If the dark, sunken spots are strictly at the bottom of the fruit, irrigate your 2-acre plot regularly to keep soil moisture even, and spray **Calcium Nitrate** (5 grams per liter of water). 

If the spots are on the leaves and fruits with yellow borders, spray **Copper Oxychloride** (3 grams/liter) or **Mancozeb** (2 grams/liter) every 7–10 days. 

Always pluck out heavily infected leaves and avoid overhead watering to stop the disease from spreading. Please tell me if the spots are on the leaves or the bottom of the fruit so I can give you exact steps!

Hello! Black spots on tomatoes in Ernakulam's humid climate are usually caused by fungal diseases like Early Blight or Bacterial Spot. 

First, immediately pluck off infected leaves or fruits and burn/bury them away from your 1-acre field to stop the spread. Spray **Mancozeb 75% WP** (2 grams per liter of water) or **Copper Oxychloride** (3 grams per liter) thoroughly on the plants, repeating after 7–10 days if necessary. 

Avoid overhead watering to keep the leaves dry, and ensure good spacing between plants for proper airflow. If the black spots are only at the bottom of the fruit, it could be a calcium deficiency (Blossom End Rot)—let me know where the spots are appearing!

crop_diagnoses.symptoms: Pale yellow to light-green chlorotic patches appear on the upper surface of the leaf. Affected areas may turn brown and dry up as the disease progresses.
crop_diagnoses.recommended_actions:
1. Prune and safely dispose of infected lower leaves to improve air circulation.
2. Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (2.5 grams per liter of water) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2 grams per liter of water).
3. If infection is severe, apply Difenoconazole 25 EC (1 ml per liter of water).
4. Avoid overhead irrigation to keep foliage dry.
crop_diagnoses.prevention:
1. Maintain wide spacing between plants for good airflow.
2. Avoid leaf wetness by using drip irrigation.
3. Regularly prune bottom leaves touching the soil.
4. Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.

crop_diagnoses.symptoms: Dark brown to black circular lesions with distinct concentric rings ('target' appearance) surrounded by yellow chlorotic halos on the leaf blade.
crop_diagnoses.recommended_actions: Prune and destroy infected leaves to reduce spore spread. Apply suitable protective fungicides such as Mancozeb (2-2.5 g/L) or Copper Oxychloride (3 g/L). Avoid overhead watering and keep the leaves dry.
crop_diagnoses.prevention: Rotate crops every 2-3 years with non-solanaceous crops. Ensure wide plant spacing for good airflow. Apply organic mulch around the plant base to stop soil splash onto leaves.

crop_diagnoses.symptoms: Prominent dark brown to black circular spots on the leaf surface surrounded by yellowish halos. Smaller dark specks are also scattered around the main necrotic lesions.
crop_diagnoses.recommended_actions: Remove and destroy infected leaves to reduce spore build-up. Spray systemic or contact fungicides such as Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L of water) or Mancozeb (2 g/L of water). Ensure lower leaves are also covered during spraying.
crop_diagnoses.prevention: Improve field drainage and maintain adequate plant spacing for proper air circulation. Avoid overhead watering to keep the foliage dry, and clean up plant debris after harvest.

crop_diagnoses.symptoms: Dark brown to black circular lesions on the leaf surrounded by yellow chlorotic halos. Smaller speckles and spot expansion visible across the leaf surface.
crop_diagnoses.recommended_actions: 1. Remove and destroy heavily infected leaves immediately to prevent spore spread. 2. Spray Mancozeb (2.5 g per liter of water) or Copper Oxychloride (3 g per liter of water). 3. Avoid overhead watering; water at the base of the plant to keep foliage dry.
crop_diagnoses.prevention: 1. Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops. 2. Apply organic mulch around the plant base to prevent soil splash onto lower leaves. 3. Maintain wide plant spacing to improve air circulation.

crop_diagnoses.symptoms: Leaf distortion, severe crinkling and puckering, characteristic light and dark green mosaic mottling, and brownish necrotic patches on affected leaf tissues.
crop_diagnoses.recommended_actions: Carefully remove and destroy infected plants immediately by burning or deep burial to prevent viral spread. Wash hands thoroughly with soap and disinfect tools using a 10% bleach solution or trisodium phosphate before touching healthy plants.
crop_diagnoses.prevention: Sow certified virus-free seeds and choose mosaic-resistant tomato varieties. Strictly avoid using tobacco products near tomato crops. Practice weed management and rotate crops with non-solanaceous plants.

crop_diagnoses.disease: Not a rice crop (Pothos / Money Plant detected)
crop_diagnoses.symptoms: The uploaded photo shows a potted indoor houseplant (Pothos / Money Plant) instead of a rice crop. The plant appears healthy with vibrant light-green foliage.
crop_diagnoses.recommended_actions: Please upload a clear photograph of your actual rice crop (leaves, stem, or panicle) for an accurate disease diagnosis.
crop_diagnoses.prevention: For healthy houseplant care, ensure proper drainage and moderate indirect sunlight. For rice crops, maintain field sanitation and follow balanced NPK fertilizer management.

crop_diagnoses.symptoms: Vibrant lime-green leaves with good turgidity. No visible signs of fungal spots, bacterial lesions, nutrient deficiency, or pest infestation.
crop_diagnoses.recommended_actions: Continue current care routine. Ensure the plant receives adequate bright, indirect sunlight and is potted in a well-draining soil medium.
crop_diagnoses.prevention: Avoid overwatering; allow the top layer of soil to dry out between waterings. Clean leaves periodically with a damp cloth to remove dust.

disease_alerts.recommended_action: Apply copper-based fungicide weekly. Remove infected leaves.
Improve air circulation. Apply neem oil spray.
Use yellow sticky traps. Apply imidacloprid if severe.
